1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable line spacing, though letter spacing appears default rather than notably generous.

2.why: No italics, all-caps instructional text, or dense paragraphs appear anywhere; all copy is short sentence-case lines.

3.why: Only desktop-width screenshots were provided, so mobile rendering cannot be confirmed, although the narrow single-column card layout suggests it would adapt.

4.why: Every instruction is a single short plain sentence, e.g. 'Use an authenticator app for payment approvals.'

5.why: The six-digit code field has no placeholder or sample format, and the pre-filled login values are actual entries rather than illustrative examples.

6.why: No screen requires reading more than a sentence or two; the only longer texts are optional fine-print notes about testing and logs.

7.why: The 32-character setup secret is rendered as ordinary text in a highlighted box so it can be selected and copied, but no dedicated copy button is provided.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent is shown; the page explicitly instructs 'Choose manual entry and enter this setup secret.'

9.why: The screenshots show plain inputs with no visible autofill cues, and attributes such as one-time-code autocomplete cannot be verified from images.

10.why: Each screen has a bold heading naming the current step and one solid blue primary button, but there is no explicit step indicator or progress display.

11.why: Every screen asks for exactly one main action (verify, set up, or confirm), with 'Log out' clearly styled as a secondary option.

12.why: Progress is only implied by the next screen's heading and a debug-style 'Logs' panel; the main UI never plainly confirms what happened (e.g. 'identity verified') and the failure message is vague.

13.why: After the wrong code the user can immediately retry with no lockout or penalty visible, but there are no reveal, hide, or re-request code controls.

14.why: The only error shown, 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.', is non-blaming but never states what the problem actually was.

15.why: No countdown or session timer is visible anywhere, yet the codes are described as 'time-bound', so entry time is inherently limited by the rotating TOTP window.
